      02Define

      The real blockers are finding a time and seeing who's in

      Problem statement

      Friend groups struggle to turn "let's go" into a confirmed plan. In the LINE chat, finding a time is slow, nobody can see who's in, and place info is often wrong. So one person ends up chasing everyone.

      Who I designed for

      Today's journey

      Tap a stage. The two lows are where Huddle has to win.

      The job, and the questions it raised

      Core job to be done

      When my friends say "let's hang out", I want to quickly lock a time and place most of us can make, so the plan actually happens without me chasing everyone.

      Tap a question to see its ideas. Rresearch Bborrowed Gmarket gap

      Five rules every screen had to follow

      • Time is the #1 pain. Place is rarely the blocker.

      • The app nudges the quiet ones, so Mint doesn't have to.

      • Planners already lock with whoever confirmed. Huddle does it on purpose.

      • 20 of 21 planned their last outing in LINE.

      • Hours at the chosen time and cost per person, upfront.

      07Reflection

      Research changed the brief

      What I learned

      The biggest pain wasn't in the brief. The best features copy what people already do by hand. Cutting was harder than adding. AI drafts fast. I still checked every count.

      Not done yet

      • A bigger sample beyond my own network
      • Check LINE API and place data access
      • Thai copy pass

      +Appendix

      Research questions, decisions and deliverables

      5 questions I'd ask stakeholders

      Before any design, I'd want these answered. Hover a card for why.

      01 · Goals

      What are the main business objectives for Huddle, and what user problems are we aiming to solve?

      Why I'd ask: So I can balance what users need with what the business needs, and know which problems matter most.

      02 · Audience

      Who is our primary target audience, and what do we currently know about their needs and behaviours?

      Why I'd ask: I have assumptions about our users. I want to know which ones research already backs, and which still need checking.

      03 · Success

      How will we measure Huddle’s success after launch, and over what timeframe?

      Why I'd ask: Which numbers would tell us we're solving the right problem, for users and for the business?

      04 · MVP scope

      Given the limited timeline, what should be prioritised for the MVP, and what can be considered for future releases?

      Why I'd ask: Which needs come first, given the research, what's feasible, and the time we have.

      05 · Constraints

      What are the key technical constraints, and how much flexibility do we have to balance simplicity with functionality?

      Why I'd ask: Knowing the trade-offs early helps me design something useful that's still realistic to build.

      Who I'd interview

      Thai 20–30s who planned or joined a group outing in the last 3 months. Both planners and joiners, ideally from the same friend group.

      1. Walk me through your last outing.
      2. Where did it get stuck? What did you do?
      3. How did you pick the place?
      4. How did you know who was coming?
      5. What makes you reply fast, or leave it on read?
